Text: Which of these is the strongest password?
Explanation: A strong password should be long, difficult to guess, and not based on common words or simple patterns.

Options.Text: Password123
H0rse!Staple!Rain?92
qwerty

Text: You receive an email from your bank asking you to verify your account. What is the biggest red flag?
Explanation: Banks do not usually ask users to click links in unexpected emails and enter full login credentials. A suspicious sender address is a major warning sign.

Options.Text: It uses your full name
The sender address is unusual and not your bank's official domain
The email uses your bank's logo

Text: True or false: It is safe to reuse the same strong password across several important accounts.
Explanation: Even a strong password becomes risky if reused. If one account is compromised, attackers may try the same password on other services.

Options.Text: True
False

Text: Which of these are signs that a message could be a phishing attempt?
Explanation: Phishing messages often use urgency, suspicious links, unexpected attachments, or requests for sensitive information.

Options.Text: The message pressures you to act immediately
The link goes to a strange or misspelled domain
The sender asks for your password or one-time code
The email contains a professional-looking logo

Text: You find a USB drive in a university computer lab. What is the safest thing to do?
Explanation: Unknown USB devices can contain malware or be used to compromise a device. They should not be plugged into personal or work computers.

Options.Text: Plug it in to check who it belongs to
Hand it to IT support or lost property without opening it
Open the files but avoid downloading anything

Text: A message appears to come from your manager asking you to send a one-time passcode urgently. What should you do?
Explanation: One-time passcodes and MFA codes should never be shared. Urgent requests should be verified through a trusted channel.

Options.Text: Send the code because the request came from your manager
Refuse to share the code and verify the request through a trusted contact method
Send the code only if the message includes your name

Text: Which of the following are good password security practices?
Explanation: Strong password security includes using unique passwords, avoiding reuse, and using a password manager where appropriate.

Options.Text: Use a unique password for each important account
Reuse one strong password across all accounts
Use a reputable password manager to store complex passwords
Base all passwords on your name and date of birth so they are easy to remember

Text: True or false: A website using HTTPS always means the website is safe and legitimate.
Explanation: HTTPS encrypts the connection, but it does not prove that the website itself is trustworthy. Phishing sites can also use HTTPS.

Options.Text: True
False

Text: You receive an email saying your account will be suspended unless you click a link immediately. What is the safest response?
Explanation: Urgency is a common phishing technique. The safest response is to avoid the link and check the account through the official website or app.

Options.Text: Click the link quickly before the account is suspended
Ignore the email completely and never check the account
Go directly to the official website or app instead of using the email link

Text: Which action best reduces the risk of a device being compromised through outdated software?
Explanation: Software updates often include security patches that fix known vulnerabilities. Delaying them can leave devices exposed.

Options.Text: Install software updates when they are available from trusted sources
Only update software if the device becomes slow
Avoid updates because they are mainly cosmetic
